_note: Presentation-only companion to service-details.json (which stays authoritative for page copy). Holds each page's hero illustration, the illustrative-situation lines and the short Not-included additions. The situation lines are written as scenarios, not client results.
ctaHeading: Start with what is happening now.
ctaBody: You do not need a technical specification or a polished scope. Start with what is happening now, what you want to work better, and any constraint that already matters.

websites.name: svc-site-anatomy
websites.caption: The structure a small-business site can follow.
websites.alt: Diagram — a small-business site structure: header, a hero with one next step, Services, Recent work, Reviews, Service area and a contact path, with Domain, Hosting and Source code marked business-held.

website-care.name: svc-care-loop
website-care.caption: Checks produce findings; a person decides what to act on.
website-care.alt: Diagram — Website Care checks: Links, Accessibility, Performance, Dependencies and Content. They produce Findings; a person does Human review; the owner approves the change; a Change log records it. Scores are evidence, not guarantees.

business-systems-automation.name: svc-handoff-before-after
business-systems-automation.caption: The same form, retyped by hand or connected.
business-systems-automation.alt: Diagram — Retyped by hand: a Form, then a person retypes it into a second tool. Connected: a Form, then an Integration, into one System of record. One source of truth.

digital-ownership-platform-administratio.name: svc-estate-inventory
digital-ownership-platform-administratio.caption: An account inventory sheet.
digital-ownership-platform-administratio.alt: Diagram — an account inventory sheet. Columns: Asset, Held by, Access, Recovery. Rows: Domain, DNS, Hosting, Source code, Email.

technology-consulting.name: svc-decision-matrix
technology-consulting.caption: Options compared on the same criteria, ending in a written recommendation.
technology-consulting.alt: Diagram — a decision matrix comparing Option A, Option B and Option C on Cost, Support, Security, Portability and Maintainability, ending in a written recommendation with next actions.

websites.includedHeading: What the work includes, and what it does not.
notIncluded: A required CMS or website platform.
A forced full rebuild when modernizing what works is the better choice.
Website Care, unless you choose it separately.
Guaranteed traffic, rankings, or marketing outcomes.
situations: A site that still follows an inherited page structure can be reorganized so a visitor can find a service and a contact path.
An owner who cannot say where the domain and hosting login live can end up with a written list of owners and named access.
A site that is hard to use on a phone can be built to be responsive and accessible, and checked in the browser before launch.

website-care.includedHeading: What care covers, and what it does not.
notIncluded: A 24x7 support or response-time commitment, unless a separate agreement says so.
A website-project bundle. Website Care is optional and separate.
Guaranteed rankings or scores. Scanner findings are evidence for human review.
situations: Small fixes that tend to wait can be handled as planned work.
The business can keep its accounts and source while LDW works through named, scoped access.
A link or accessibility scan can produce findings, and a person decides which ones are worth acting on.
website-care.railHeading: A site that stays looked after.

business-systems-automation.stepsLead: The order matters: use what already works, automate the repeated step, and build custom only where a measured gap remains.
notIncluded: An automation that becomes a competing source of truth.
Document Control or Secure Exchange as an offered customer product. Both are internal LDW work.
situations: A form submission that is retyped into another system can move through a supported integration.
A tool that nearly fits can be checked for a native feature or a configuration change before anything new is built.
An automation can be documented well enough that it could be changed or removed later.

digital-ownership-platform-administratio.includedHeading: What the work covers, and what it does not.
notIncluded: LDW holding master passwords or MFA recovery codes.
LDW becoming the permanent recovery owner.
Ongoing administration by default. It applies only where a clear recurring responsibility is agreed.
situations: The owner can come to see which accounts, providers, and recovery paths exist.
A former vendor's access can be documented and changed before anything is moved.
Ownership, recovery, and who administers what can be written down.
digital-ownership-platform-administratio.railHeading: A setup the business can recover.
digital-ownership-platform-administratio.proofHeading: Who holds the keys, in a worked example.

technology-consulting.includedHeading: What the review covers, and what it does not.
notIncluded: An open-ended engagement. Consulting does not always lead to a build.
situations: Two competing platforms can be compared on tradeoffs, with a recommendation written down.
Architecture and support can be matched to the real need instead of a bigger program.
The finding can be to leave the working system alone.
technology-consulting.roadmapAlt: Diagram — Current setup, then Findings, then Options and tradeoffs, then a Bounded roadmap with next actions. From Findings there is also a dashed branch: Leave it alone.
